summary_oneline: Add a Postgres CrewDefinition store (navigator.crew_definitions) beside CrewRedis, initialized after Redis, with a migration=True flag that copies existing Redis crews into Postgres and rehydrates crews from it.

localization.role: the only CrewDefinition store today; its 7 BotManager-used methods are the contract a Postgres store must mirror
read-side compatibility (unknown-key stripping) that Postgres reads must share
enumeration of every (tenant, name) incl. legacy global keys — the migration source iterator
builds self.crew_redis when enable_crews; where a second store is wired
startup rehydration of all tenants' crews; natural hook for 'init Redis, then Postgres, then migrate'
delete path (also half of the HTTP PUT update)
cross-worker reconciliation via list_all_crews before listing
persisted model: crew_id uuid4 str, tenant default 'global', name; extra='forbid'
closest navigator.* store pattern: default_dsn, ensure_schema, CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS navigator, ON CONFLICT upsert
lazy idempotent DDL precedent for crews; its _TABLE_RE rejects schema-qualified names
only flag gating crew-definition persistence; new backend/migration keys go here
idempotent sweep + dry_run + MigrationReport precedent for the migration loop
backend-selection precedent: explicit setting, probe, fail-closed
FEAT-621 gates: creation.sql and _load_database_bots frozen; no migration at startup (Studio scope)
pins bm.crew_redis and the CrewRedis patch target

constraints.statement: BotManager is the only production consumer of CrewRedis and uses 7 methods: save_crew, load_crew, load_crew_by_id, delete_crew, ping, get_all_crews, list_all_crews
constraints.implication: a Postgres store (or a dual-store facade) must offer exactly these with the same return conventions; handlers and other get_crew consumers stay untouched

constraints.statement: Crew identity is (tenant, name) with a secondary (tenant, crew_id) index; None normalizes to 'global'; legacy un-tenanted keys are read only for 'global'
constraints.implication: the table needs UNIQUE (tenant, name) and UNIQUE (tenant, crew_id); the migration must enumerate legacy global crews too (list_all_crews already does)

constraints.statement: Stored crews stay loadable only because CrewRedis._deserialize_crew strips unknown keys before CrewDefinition(**dict) under extra='forbid'
constraints.implication: Postgres reads must reuse the same compatibility step — extract it to a shared helper rather than duplicate it

constraints.statement: CrewDefinition keeps gaining fields (ToolNode, execution wiki, infographic theme) and a column-per-field table already caused total load failure for navigator.ai_bots
constraints.implication: store the whole model_dump(mode='json') in one jsonb column and promote only identity/listing columns

constraints.statement: Two DDL policies coexist: in-module auto-create (PgUISurfaceStore, PostgresResultStorage) and migration-files-only with no migration at startup (Studio, FEAT-621 gates scoped to the Studio stack)
constraints.implication: the spec must pick one for navigator.crew_definitions; creation.sql and BotManager._load_database_bots are byte-frozen and must not be edited

constraints.statement: PostgresResultStorage validates table names with ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$, which rejects navigator.crew_definitions
constraints.implication: do not reuse that helper; follow the PgUISurfaceStore schema-qualified DDL idiom

constraints.statement: CrewRedis is built in BotManager.__init__, before the aiohttp app and its app['database'] pool exist; default_dsn can be None
constraints.implication: the Postgres store must connect lazily (AsyncDB per call with a DSN) or be created in on_startup, and must define behaviour when no DSN is configured

constraints.statement: BotManager.load_crews runs in every gunicorn worker at startup
constraints.implication: a startup migration must be idempotent (ON CONFLICT upsert) and serialized (pg advisory lock), with per-crew error isolation and a report

constraints.statement: Persistence errors are swallowed: CrewRedis returns False/None and BotManager logs and keeps the crew memory-only
constraints.implication: a silent Postgres write failure during a 'move' could lose crews if Redis is cleaned afterwards

constraints.statement: Tests pin bm.crew_redis and patch parrot.manager.manager.CrewRedis
constraints.implication: keep the crew_redis attribute (or update test_botmanager_flags.py) and add a sibling patch target for the Postgres store

new: A Postgres CrewDefinition store in handlers/crew/ (e.g. CrewPostgres) over navigator.crew_definitions: tenant, name, crew_id, description, execution_mode, definition jsonb, created_at/updated_at timestamptz; UNIQUE (tenant, name), UNIQUE (tenant, crew_id); the 7 BotManager methods + close; save = INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tenant, name) DO UPDATE
DDL for navigator.crew_definitions (in-module ensure_schema and/or a crew_definitions_creation.sql file — U4)
A dual-store composition that initializes Redis, then Postgres, and routes reads/writes per the chosen source-of-truth policy (U1)
A migration routine (Redis -> Postgres) driven by migration=True: iterate list_all_crews + load_crew, upsert, per-crew report, optional dry_run, advisory lock (U2, U3)
Config keys following the CREW_RESULT_STORAGE* precedent (e.g. CREW_DEFINITION_STORAGE, CREW_DEFINITION_PG_DSN, CREW_DEFINITION_MIGRATION) with BotManager kwarg overrides (U5)
A shared deserialization helper extracted from CrewRedis._strip_unknown_keys/_deserialize_crew
Unit tests with a fake AsyncDB (PgUISurfaceStore pattern), a live test gated on a DSN env var, and migration tests

modified.change: construct and call the dual store; run the migration from load_crews when enabled
delegate to the shared compatibility helper
add the crew-definition backend / DSN / migration keys next to it

untouched: CrewHandler HTTP surface (/api/v1/crew GET/PUT/DELETE; no PATCH added here)

patterns.pattern: PgUISurfaceStore: AsyncDB('pg', dsn=default_dsn) per call, _DDL_STATEMENTS with CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS navigator, ensure_schema tolerating races, ON CONFLICT upsert
migrate_store: idempotent sweep, per-item try/except into a report, dry_run never writes
Config flag + constructor override (FEAT-042 BotManager flags; CREW_RESULT_STORAGE* naming)
Studio backend selection: explicit setting, read-only probe, fail closed when Postgres is required

risks.risk: Redis and Postgres diverge when both are written/read
risks.impact: a crew edited in one store resurrects or disappears via sync_crews
risks.mitigation: one source of truth after migration (U1)

risks.risk: Concurrent startup migration in every worker
risks.impact: duplicate work, lock contention, racing deletes if 'move' cleans Redis
risks.mitigation: ON CONFLICT upsert + pg advisory lock, or explicit one-shot trigger (U3)

risks.risk: Deleting Redis keys after a swallowed Postgres write failure
risks.mitigation: verify by re-reading from Postgres before any Redis delete; keep Redis by default (U2)

risks.risk: Stored crews that no longer validate (model validators, not unknown keys)
risks.mitigation: per-crew error isolation and a report

risks.risk: Naive vs tz-aware timestamps (CrewRedis writes datetime.utcnow())
risks.mitigation: treat naive as UTC on write

unknowns.question: Once Postgres is enabled, which store is the source of truth for reads and writes?
plausible_answers: Postgres primary for reads and writes; Redis read-only fallback for crews not yet migrated
Dual-write to both; read Postgres first, then Redis
Postgres only after migration; Redis no longer written
unknowns.user_answer: Postgres primary: reads and writes go to Postgres; Redis is a read-only fallback for crews not yet migrated.

unknowns.question: Does 'mover' mean deleting the Redis keys after a verified copy, or copying and keeping Redis?
plausible_answers: Copy, re-read from Postgres to verify, then delete the Redis keys
Copy and mark the Redis keys as migrated (rename/TTL)
unknowns.user_answer: Copy, verify, delete: copy into Postgres, re-read each crew from Postgres to confirm it, then delete its Redis keys.

unknowns.question: Where does the migration run?
plausible_answers: In BotManager.load_crews at startup when migration=True, serialized with a pg advisory lock
As an explicit one-shot (CLI / method) never called at startup, per the FEAT-621 policy
Both: the startup hook and the CLI call the same idempotent function
unknowns.user_answer: Startup + lock: run in BotManager.load_crews when migration=True, serialized across workers with a pg advisory lock and idempotent via upsert.

Reuse default_dsn and ENABLE_CREWS; only a migration kwarg

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence and the request already fixes the architecture (Redis + Postgres store + migration flag); the open forks are policy choices (U1-U5) that the Q&A phase can settle without a brainstorm.
